question.problem:
A survey concerning the number of online music subscriptions per household in a certain town is carried out. The results were given below. Based on this data, if the random variable $X$ represents the number of subscriptions in a randomly selected household, what is $\text{SD}[X]?$

| Music subscriptions | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Households | $1$ | $12$ | $48$ | $64$ |
question.worked_solution:
The standard deviation of a random variable $X$ is defined as

$$
\text{SD}[X]=\sqrt{\text{Var}[X]},
$$

where the variance can be computed using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

First, we need to compute the probability mass function $f(x).$ To do this, we divide each frequency by the total, which is $1+12+48+64=125.$ We get the following result:

| $x$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{1}{125}$ | $\frac{12}{125}$ | $\frac{48}{125}$ | $\frac{64}{125}$ |

Now, we compute $\text{E}[X]$ by summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =0\cdot f(0)+1\cdot f(1)+2\cdot f(2)+3\cdot f(3) \\  & =0(\frac{1}{125})+1(\frac{12}{125})+2(\frac{48}{125})+3(\frac{64}{125}) \\  & =\frac{12}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}].$ Summing up the products of each value of ${X}^{2}$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={0}^{2}\cdot f(0)+{1}^{2}\cdot f(1)+{2}^{2}\cdot f(2)+{3}^{2}\cdot f(3) \\  & =0(\frac{1}{125})+1(\frac{12}{125})+4(\frac{48}{125})+9(\frac{64}{125}) \\  & =\frac{156}{25}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{156}{25}-{(\frac{12}{5})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{156}{25}-\frac{144}{25} \\  & =\frac{12}{25}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{SD}[X] & =\sqrt{\text{Var}[X]} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{12}{25}} \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
